I WAS BORN IN THE CARIBBEAN, EDUCATED IN ENGLAND, AND I OBTAINED A DOUBLE MAJOR IN ANTHROPOLOGY AND ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF TORONTO. I HAVE LIVED AND WORKED IN TRINIDAD, THE UK, THE UAE, AND CANADA BEFORE MAKING TAMPA MY HOME ABOUT TEN YEARS AGO. I SETTLED IN SOUTH TAMPA WITH MY HUSBAND. DURING THE PANDEMIC, I TURNED TO ONLINE LEARNING COMPLETING WORK IN GLOBAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY CITIES TO STAY ON TOP OF EMERGING ISSUES. WHEREVER I'VE CALLED HOME I'VE ENDEAVORED TO TRANSFER ENVIRONMENTAL PASSION INTO GRASSROOTS ACTION. I'VE DONE QUITE A BIT OF COMMUNITY OUTREACH SERVING FOR SEVERAL YEARS AS FOUNDING MEMBER FOR GRASSROOTS NONPROFIT CALLED GREEN 13. THIS WAS IN TORONTO. I WAS ALSO INTERNING AS A COMMUNITY COORDINATOR WHERE WE FACILITATED THE IMPLEMENTATION AND PROGRAMMING OF A MUNICIPAL CARBON CHALLENGE INITIATIVE, AND THIS WAS FOR A PROVINCIAL CANDIDATE. ALSO PERFORMED OUTREACH AND MARKETING FOR ANOTHER NONPROFIT CALLED FOR OUR GRANDCHILDREN. I SERVED ON ALSO MY CONDOMINIUM WASTE DIVERSION INITIATIVE COMMITTEE AND ALSO VOLUNTEERED WITH LOCAL COUNCILWOMEN DURING LOCAL ELECTIONS. THIS WAS IN TORONTO AS WELL. BUT HERE IN TAMPA, I'M HONORED TO SERVE THE BAYSHORE BEAUTIFUL NEIGHBORHOOD ASSOCIATION, PRIMARILY AS THE COMMITTEE CHAIR FOR ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY AND NOW AS VICE PRESIDENT CURRENT FOR THESE TWO YEARS. IN THE BBNA, WE ALSO PARTNERED IN 2023 WITH THE MAYOR'S FREE TREE GIVEAWAY. WE ONLY COULD HOUSE ABOUT I THINK 70 TREES ON OUR PROPERTIES, AND WE HAD SO MANY MORE APPLICANTS THAT WE COULD NOT FULFILL THE DEMAND BECAUSE OF ALL THE DEMAND FOR THE TREES. SO I WANT TO SERVE ON THE NATURAL RESOURCES ADVISORY COMMITTEE BECAUSE I BELIEVE IN TRANSPARENT LOCAL GOVERNANCE, OPEN COMMUNICATION, AND DIRECT COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND PARTNERSHIPS. BECAUSE I'VE LIVED AND WORKED IN DIFFERENT COUNTRIES, I LIVED IN LARGE CITIES, SMALL TOWNS, AND I CAN SAY THAT TAMPA'S GROWTH AND RESOURCE CHALLENGES ARE NOT UNIQUE. ANY MEDIUM OR LARGE CITY EXPERIENCING RAPID EXPANSION THAT WE HAVE FACES IMMENSE PRESSURE ON ITS NATURAL RESOURCES. I BELIEVE THAT ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES DO NOT EXIST IN SILOS. WE HAVE TO PROTECT OUR NATURAL RESOURCES. IT'S NOT JUST ABOUT BUDGET, IT'S ABOUT ACHIEVING SOMETHING LASTING WITH THE RESOURCES WE ALREADY HAVE. I BELIEVE WITH COLLABORATION, OPEN DIALOGUE AND CREATIVE PARTNERSHIPS, WE CAN BRING THIS ISSUE TO THE BOARD. THANK YOU FOR YOUR TIME.

MAYOR CASTOR'S 30 BY 30 INITIATIVE IS LAUDABLE, BUT I FEEL SO MUCH MORE CAN AND SHOULD BE DONE TO PROTECT OUR EXISTING TREES AND OUR CANOPY. WE'VE BEEN DESIGNATED AS A TREE CITY FOR DECADES, AND I THINK WE CAN AND SHOULD DO MORE. IN THE LAST TEN YEARS, I'VE TAKEN ACTION TO TURN OUR LAWN FROM GRASS TO 90 PERCENT NATIVES. I ACTIVELY ENGAGE WITH OUR NEIGHBORS TO ANSWER QUESTIONS ABOUT GARDENS, IMPORTANCE OF TREES, AND BE AN ADVOCATE FOR THE ENVIRONMENT IN GENERAL. THANK YOU FOR YOUR TIME.
